ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Human albinism is an autosomal recessive genetic disease. The pedigree chart of a certain patient's family is shown in Figure A. It is known that a certain method can make the normal gene A show one band, while the albinism gene a shows another different band. This method was used to analyze each individual in the above family, and the presence or absence of bands and their positions are marked in Figure B. Question: What are the genotypes of individuals 2–5 respectively?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The genotypes of individuals 2–5 are respectively Aa, AA, AA, and aa.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A is a pedigree chart, in which number 2 is an unaffected female, number 3 is an unaffected male, number 4 is an unaffected female, and number 5 is a female affected by albinism. Figure B shows the band detection results for individuals 1–13. Number 2 has bands at both band 1 and band 2 positions, numbers 3 and 4 have bands only at the band 1 position, and number 5 has a band only at the band 2 position. Reasoning: The stem states that the normal gene A and the albinism gene a will show bands at different positions. Since albinism is an autosomal recessive genetic disease, the genotype of an affected individual must be aa. In Figure A, number 5 has albinism, and in Figure B, number 5 has only band 2, so band 2 corresponds to the albinism gene a, and band 1 corresponds to the normal gene A. Thus individuals with both band 1 and band 2 are Aa; individuals with only band 1 are AA; individuals with only band 2 are aa. Therefore number 2 is Aa, number 3 is AA, number 4 is AA, and number 5 is aa.
